articles.headline: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Training on Compute Islands

A single run could mix accelerator generations and vendors as each island runs on its own schedule. Older generations or less common chips could also participate in a frontier run. One risk with this model is that integrity and safety may become harder when models are trained across providers, as one faulty or compromised site can quietly degrade or tamper with models in ways that are harder to trace.

articles.headline: GPU-accelerated Weight Teleportation

This is achieved using a co-designed compression/decompression pipeline with GPU-accelerated parallel processing, utilizing efficient codecs like LZ4 and Snappy, combined with a Zstd layer.

articles.headline: Harness 2: executing agent code as it streams
articles.blurb: Framer's Harness 2 significantly upgrades the agent's execution process, allowing entire workflows in one program, achieving up to 33% cost reduction and 20% faster execution. This is done by executing JavaScript as it streams in, avoiding multiple model calls and using eager execution and early cancellation to enhance efficiency. The redesign also replaces DSL with method calls for real-time updates, making task execution streamlined for both in-app and external agents, reducing tool steps by 43% and cached input tokens by 39% per message.

articles.headline: What Is Quantum Advantage Actually Worth?
articles.blurb: Nearly all roadmaps point to a utility-scale quantum computer being developed around 2030. Despite this, there is little confidence or clarity on how these machines will actually be useful. The consensus is now that they'll first be used for breaking cryptography. The second most concrete answer is to use them to generate simulation data for AI labs' science models. This post looks at how else quantum computing could be applied and where all the revenue will come from.

articles.headline: China publicly discloses plan for a lunar landing within three years
articles.blurb: Chinese space officials have confirmed the country's plans to land astronauts on the Moon within three years. The landings will involve a lunar-orbit rendezvous similar to what NASA did with the Apollo program. China and the US are racing to land astronauts on the lunar surface, as it would be a major geopolitical win. Both countries are also building capabilities to establish a long-term presence at the Moon's South Pole.

articles.headline: Scaling Git at OpenAI
articles.blurb: OpenAI's monorepo's size and demands increased at a staggering pace over the last year, necessitating a revamp of the AI lab's source control system. Its technical staff built Pando, a new backend for Git repositories optimized for concurrent pushes to many branches and to maximize read throughput. The team implemented the backend without interrupting any engineering work or changing how the team uses Git. Pando cut median push latency in production by nearly 5x, and it now delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day.

articles.headline: Why Agents Are Soon Only Going to Have 1 Tool
articles.blurb: Agents are collapsing their entire tool catalog into one 'exec' tool. This allows models to write short scripts that chain, combine, and await actions inside isolated sandboxes. Models can now reliably combine and chain dependent actions in a single pass. In the previous standard tool-calling model, agents could only perform single actions, but the exec tool allows them to perform multiple actions.

articles.headline: Our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside
articles.blurb: Organizations are losing attention as everyone within is doing something they think is useful, but all that work draws on the same limited capacity to understand, review, and decide. Just because work exists doesn't mean it's the right thing to do. Output is not proof of value. A working implementation only means that something can be built, not that it should be - some changes have negative value.

articles.headline: The value of open source
articles.blurb: People open source projects for various reasons. Some do it to build a company or product, others do it performatively, and some ship code just for the love of the game. Open source was never free to copy, and the code was never the moat. AI can remake a product, but it can't provide the rest of the value a company generates. The technology is helping maintainers ship and fix problems faster.

It reads both content and layout across full designs like multi-page decks, writes and runs small pieces of code, and inspects results before each next step. Brush is in beta for Canva Pro subscribers, with Brand Kit support and better image-heavy layout handling planned.

The red, white, black, and gold system also features a wave pattern, a horizontal split evoking the Amstel River, and three coins representing the founders, city, and waterway. Already a Red Dot winner, the identity is rolling out across 11 markets, with all remaining territories due to transition by the end of 2027.

articles.headline: Design is more than creation
articles.blurb: Design is the deliberate process of deciding how something should work, respond, and be experienced, not simply the act of producing something that looks convincing. Conditions such as accessibility needs, localization, unpredictable content, failures, and different input methods should shape software from the beginning rather than being treated as edge cases to fix afterward. AI makes polished software dramatically faster to create, but that speed increases the importance of understanding which decisions were made, which assumptions they rely on, and whether they survive contact with reality.

articles.headline: How We're Training a Figma-Fluent Editing Model
articles.blurb: Specialized post-training lets Figma's first-party editing model compete with frontier models on precise, iterative edits to existing designs. A Llama 3.3 70B model trained on 250,000+ examples first became competitive with top models, but imitation learning limited generalization, so Figma now invests in reinforcement learning. Since beta, typical tasks run about 20% faster, users rate results 33% higher, and they undo the agent's work 60% less often.

articles.headline: Experience Design: Dropping the “User” from “User Experience”
articles.blurb: AI agents complicate the traditional definition of UX because people may increasingly accomplish goals without directly interacting with the companies, applications, and interfaces involved. Experience design provides a broader framing that includes traditional UX while also considering digital systems used by agents acting on humans' behalf and journeys involving multiple human and nonhuman actors. People's goals remain central, but designers must now consider experiences in which the immediate user of a product may be an AI rather than a person.

Copy must fit its space, CTAs must match the reader's decision stage, and a final proofread should test every link and QR code.

articles.headline: Visa signs digital payments deal with Senegal
articles.blurb: Visa and Senegal's Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Affairs have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) establishing a two-year framework for strategic collaboration to support Senegal's digital transformation ambitions.

articles.headline: Fashion retailer Resolve says hackers stole payment card information
articles.blurb: Revolve told the SEC that attackers accessed multiple systems and used automated methods to obtain names, contact details, and card numbers and expiration dates from customers who stored payment data online. Texas regulators recorded 127,200 affected residents. Vermont reported 1,328. Revolve notified law enforcement, hired a cybersecurity firm, and said operations and finances were unaffected.

articles.headline: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
articles.blurb: A suspected cyber-attack switched refrigeration evaporators to defrost mode at supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Finland. Freezer temperatures reportedly reached 50°C, forcing stores to discard spoiled food. A Delhaize branch reported €100,000 in losses. Sabcobel said affected units need physical changes. Remote internet-connected maintenance remains part of the operating model.

articles.headline: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
articles.blurb: IBM reported four Langflow vulnerabilities affecting versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8. Two are critical and require no account: CVE-2026-93680 bypasses authentication, while CVE-2026-110186 permits arbitrary code execution through MCP tool enumeration. A public Metasploit module already enumerates Langflow MCP tools without credentials. Version 1.13.0 is the only fix. It disables automatic login by default. IBM has not published a workaround.

articles.headline: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
articles.blurb: Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP requests in Q3 2026. Short attacks under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps rose 208% year over year, while attacks above 1 Tbps fell 69% from Q2. CLDAP floods dropped 99.5%. DNS amplification rose 215%, and UDP floods rose 122%. The United States was the most-attacked country, followed by China and Indonesia. Canada rose from 16th to 6th, and Israel to 10th. IoT botnets remain active, with Mirai-classified traffic peaking at 57.23 PB in August.

articles.headline: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
articles.blurb: Researchers at Parameter Labs discovered a complex attack chain that could let attackers create malicious pages using ChatGPT's HTML Previews (formerly Canvas). The exploit begins by using the MathLive JavaScript library to create a new iframe that could load scripts from YouTube despite OpenAI's CSP policy. That iframe could then use YouTube's oEmbed endpoint to access OpenAI API endpoints and steal private data from anyone who accesses the ChatGPT share URL.

articles.headline: Turning the Valve - Exploiting RCE and LPE in the Steam Platform
articles.blurb: Atredis researchers found four local privilege escalation flaws and two remote code execution bugs in Steam for Windows. The LPE paths abused Steam's SYSTEM service through install-script allowlists, module loading, secure-desktop input forwarding, and driver installation. The remote bugs affected Steam-to-Steam synchronization messages: stack overflows in download-schedule and app-status handlers, plus an uninitialized-memory leak of steamclient64 pointers. The researchers combined the leak with an overflow to build a zero-click RCE using a ROP chain. They reported the issues to Valve through HackerOne. The bugs are patched or past the disclosure timeline, and proof-of-concept code is public.

articles.headline: PyPCAPKit (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: PyPCAPKit is an open-source Python library for parsing, constructing, and analyzing network packets and PCAP files, with DictDumper as its formatted output dumper.

articles.headline: Wake and Break (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: Wake and Break is a PSP (Platform Security Processor) exploit for AMD navi31 cards that will disable PSP's firmware signature check so that the card will load unsigned IP firmware.

articles.headline: MCPTrace (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: MCPTrace is a Volatility 3 plugin for extracting MCP/JSON-RPC message candidates from Windows and Linux memory dumps.

articles.headline: Securing Internet Critical Software: How We Could Have Backdoored Bash
articles.blurb: Researchers at Hacktron discovered a command injection vulnerability in GNU Savannah that let them gain root and take over user accounts, including a Bash maintainer. The vulnerability stemmed from the GPG key validator inserting a user's email address directly into commands it executed without sanitizing the input. The attackers utilized this vulnerability to install a webshell, read the database password, set their account to a superuser, impersonate other users, and also escalate privileges by exploiting GemOver(lay).

articles.headline: Cyberattack Hits Rosstat as Hackers Claim Huge Data Theft
articles.blurb: The Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow hacking groups claimed they stole 23TB of data from Russia's state statistics agency, Rosstat. The attackers claim to have stolen data on Russian wartime losses, demographic and economic statistics, and documents marked “for official use only.” Rosstat denied that any databases or legally protected information was leaked.

articles.headline: Our Latest Defenses Against Evolving Web Scams
articles.blurb: The Google Chrome team released several new features to further harden the Enhanced Protection mode of Private Browsing. Chrome will now display warnings when a user browses to a suspicious or risky site (depending on confidence level) and provide LLM-based scam detection. Chrome also implemented LLM-based ClickFix attack detection.

articles.blurb: Google's Cloud VRP now pays up to $250,000 for exploits that achieve roles/owner or full IAM control over arbitrary Google Cloud tenants, or code execution in its Borg production infrastructure, without existing access, stolen credentials, or user interaction.

articles.headline: Over 1,000 GitLab servers exposed to active attacks
articles.blurb: More than 1,000 internet-facing GitLab servers remain vulnerable to a maximum-severity remote code execution flaw that attackers are actively exploiting. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97229, affects GitLab's CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler and can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code. CISA has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

articles.headline: WorkOS discloses AI-assisted data security incident
articles.blurb: WorkOS disclosed unauthorized access to an internal sales application on October 30, exposing business contact information, customer account histories, and excerpts from customer communications. The company identified the use of an AI-assisted offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts. It has disabled external access to the affected application while it investigates the full impact.

articles.blurb: Google Cloud published a guide demonstrating how to connect Gemini Enterprise agents to Snowflake using the Model Context Protocol and Agent Development Kit. articles.blurb: Microsoft and Lumen are expanding their collaboration to help enterprises connect data, applications, and infrastructure across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters.
